eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Six
subtitle: Lesson 62 · Data Types, Strings, Dates and Modern T-SQL

eyebrow: FOR JSON AUTO: let SQL Server infer the shape
caption: One JSON array, one object per row.

eyebrow: AUTO infers nesting from a join
code:
SELECT TOP 3 p.Name AS ProductName,
       psc.Name AS SubcategoryName
FROM Production.Product AS p
JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory AS psc
  ON psc.ProductSubcategoryID = p.ProductSubcategoryID
FOR JSON AUTO;
caption: Nesting follows the join shape automatically.

eyebrow: FOR JSON PATH: explicit control via dotted aliases
code:
SELECT TOP 3 p.ProductID,
  p.Name AS [Product.Name],
  p.ListPrice AS [Product.Price],
  psc.Name AS [Product.Subcategory]
FROM Production.Product AS p
JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory AS psc
  ON psc.ProductSubcategoryID = p.ProductSubcategoryID
FOR JSON PATH;
caption: You control the JSON structure directly, via the alias names.

eyebrow: Dropping the array wrapper for one row
code:
SELECT TOP 1 ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
ORDER BY ProductID
FOR JSON PATH, WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER;
caption: Plain object instead of a one-element array.

subtitle: The reverse operation -- JSON, parsed back into rows.
